title_original: Festival Brisons le silence: Cléo-Nikita Thomasson – Faire trace
excerpt_original: Le 23 novembre à Lyon, la Maison des Femmes de Lyon - Espace Tonkin (Villeurbanne) accueillera l'exposition La Chronique du non-dit de Cleo-Nikita Thomasson. Elle détaille son projet. Cet article Festival Brisons le silence: Cléo-Nikita Thomasson – Faire trace est apparu en…

blocks.text: On November 23 in Lyon, the Maison des Femmes de Lyon—Espace Tonkin (Villeurbanne) will host the exhibition La Chronique du non-dit by Cleo-Nikita Thomasson. She provides details about her project.

“In 2021, with too much time on my hands and no work due to Covid, I walked through the doors of a charity: the only women-only daytime protection centre for women who are victims of violence, isolation and precarious living conditions. I then spent two years going there every week to learn about and discover the world of community organisations. This experience moved me deeply; I met people who became friends and allies for future projects.

As with my documentary projects, I realised the crucial role that personal experience plays in social activism: how can I bridge the gap between culture and the community sector? How can I expose and highlight issues, and bring together precariousness and the elite? How can I bring these worlds together and give a voice to the invisible? How can I establish myself within the cultural sector to take action? Where is the bridge?

In 2023, I co-wrote a community project with two others aimed at creating support groups for victims of sexist, sexual and gender-based violence (VSS). For a year, I wove a web of connections and carved out a place for myself in the city to carry out this project as best I could.

At the same time, I continued to nurture my personal projects, even though first-person narratives for institutions and galleries appealed to me less and less… I wanted to create spaces where women could speak out and tell their stories in their own words and through their own eyes. I imagined women’s centres in rural areas, spaces for self-expression with time for healing… utopian budgets, dreams of creating resource books that could help other women: those who are listened to and those who listen – a virtuous circle to which I cling.

To bear witness, to show, to demand, to help… verbs replace words; the need to do and to act keeps me from letting go of this thread I am weaving. I’m discovered that, like photography projects, socio-cultural projects share the same temporal dimension: everything takes time… goals take a long time to achieve, and we must hold on to hope even when our social experiences leave us battered, in tears and at our wits’ end in the face of so much injustice and such urgent need. That feeling of putting a Band Aid on a leaky faucet, wanting to burn down all the police stations, wanting to move faster and harder, yet also needing rest to keep moving forward, defending one’s vision and values, and holding on to one’s ethics so as not to give up.
Then I trained as a photographer-facilitator with the Réseau Diagonale.

It was between Marseille, Strasbourg and Carcassonne that I discovered a tailor-made programme to learn how to create cultural protocols for vulnerable people. I learnt a great deal and also met some fabulous people. I wrote my proposal for cultural action workshops combining photography and writing, with the aim of creating collective diaries to give women a voice. And in the same year, I set sail to accompany a group of women on sailing boats in collaboration with several organisations.

Today, I’ve joined La Maison des Femmes in Lyon and have been facilitating a support group for women who have suffered female genital mutilation for the past year. It took me five years to reach my goal, and even though there is still so much to do, I am where I have always wanted to be: a photographer, facilitator, writer and researcher, documenting and bearing witness to social struggles through the arts.”
Cleo-Nikita Thomasson – La Chronique du non-dit Dans le cadre du Festival Brisons le silence à Lyon Maison des Femmes de Lyon 23 novembre à l’Espace Tonkin, Villeurbanne
